summary: Set out a six-stage deal pipeline with exit criteria linked to the week 4 scoring screen. Agreed conversion and coverage targets and a 45-day rule for stalled deals. The cycle time target needs more work before Helen and Mark sign it off.

discussion.keyPoints: Mark's deal log showed roughly 1 in 9 first meetings reach an indicative offer and the average time from first meeting to exclusivity is around 26 weeks.
Calder wants 4 platform deals a year from Fund II. Helen asked how many live opportunities that really needs at each stage.
Several deals sat untouched for months without a decision. Mark said nobody feels able to kill a deal a partner likes.

recommendations.recommendation: Use six stages: Identified, First meeting, Qualified, Indicative offer, Exclusivity, Completed. A deal only becomes Qualified with a score of 3 or more on the five-criterion screen.
Track first meeting to indicative offer and lift it from about 1 in 9 to 1 in 6.
Cut time from first meeting to exclusivity from around 26 weeks to 16 weeks.
Hold 24 qualified opportunities in the pipeline at any time to support 4 platform deals a year.
Any deal with no movement for 45 days is reviewed at the Monday pipeline meeting and either revived with a next step or parked.

actions.action: Re-stage the current deal log into the six stages

nextFocus: Choose how the pipeline is recorded and reported, and replace the Excel deal log.
nextPreparation: Bring the Excel deal log and any CRM quotes already received.

tests.question: How many qualified opportunities should we hold in the pipeline?
What did we agree about deals that stall?
Is the 16-week cycle time target agreed?
